scope: Proposition 8.3 of the manuscript “All-temperature pressure for orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses” (preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 234 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ecaeb31108feca6f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix s ∈ (−1, 1) and positive interval weights w0, . . . , wk−1. The function ℓ[s] is concave on 0 ≤ h0 ≤ · · · ≤ hk−1 < ∞. Its minimizing bias bs(h) in (8.2) is unique. On strict level data, set Bi(h, s) = Bi(h, bs(h)). Then ∂hi ℓ[s] (h) = − wi 2 Bi(h, s). (8.6) The associated supporting inequalities extend to boundary level data and are unchanged by subdivision of intervals with tied covariance levels. The function is 1/2-Lipschitz in the L1 distance between bounded nonnegative nondecreasing paths.
